newsitem.title: USA: U.S. utility ordered to pay $2 million for fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. utility ordered to pay $2 million for fire.

text.p: A California court ordered Pacific Gas & Electric Co., a unit of PG&E Corp., to pay almost $2 million in fines and restitution for causing a 1994 wildfire and neglecting to trim trees around power lines.
At a hearing in Nevada County Municipal Court, Judge Carlos Baker ordered the giant utility to pay about $1.6 million in fines and $359,500 in restitution.
PG&E was found guilty last month of causing the Aug. 7, 1994, Trauner fire in northern California that burned 500 acres, destroyed 12 houses and caused $3 million in damage.
The blaze started when a branch touched a high-voltage power line.
The utility was also found guilty by a six-man, six-woman jury of 738 misdemeanor counts involving trimming trees around power lines.
PG&E has 30 days to decide whether to appeal.

Baker also set a restitution hearing for Nov. 7 to decide whether additional restitution should be paid by PG&E to victims of the Trauner fire. The company has already paid $1.2 million in compensation to fire victims.
It was the first time PG&E had been criminally prosecuted in California for neglecting to trim trees and the 32-day trial was closely watched by other counties.
The jury found PG&E guilty of deliberately limiting its tree maintenance programme, violating a series of state laws on power line clearance and fire breaks.
Bill Roake, a spokesman for PG&E, said the company regretted the fire.
"We are committed to operating an electrical system that is safe and reliable," he said, adding the company had "one of the premier tree-trimming programmes in the country."

Asked if PG&E would appeal, Roake said the company would explore all its options. He added: "We intend to put this event behind us and focus on doing everything we can to prevent anything like this from happening again."
